sidenav_install_help_intro_generic: Khartis can be installed as a Progressive Web App. The exact labels change depending on the browser and platform.

sidenav_install_help_ios_step_3: Confirm the addition to install Khartis on your device.
sidenav_install_help_chromium_step_1: On a computer, look for the installation icon in the address bar.
sidenav_install_help_chromium_step_2: Otherwise, open the browser menu and choose 'Install application' or 'Install Khartis'.
sidenav_install_help_chromium_step_3: On Android, the option may also appear as 'Add to Home Screen'.
sidenav_install_help_safari_mac_step_2: Choose 'Add to Dock' when the option is available.

sidenav_install_help_firefox_step_1: On Android, open the menu then use the installation or add to home screen option.
sidenav_install_help_firefox_step_2: On iPhone or iPad, use the Share menu then 'Add to Home Screen'.
sidenav_install_help_firefox_step_3: On a computer, Firefox does not offer the classic PWA installation. Use Chrome, Edge or Safari instead to install Khartis.
sidenav_install_help_opera_step_2: Look for 'Install application', 'Install' or 'Add to Home Screen'.
sidenav_install_help_opera_step_3: If the option does not appear, try from Chrome, Edge or Safari.
sidenav_install_help_other_step_1: Look for an installation icon in the address bar or a dedicated entry in the browser menu.
sidenav_install_help_other_step_2: When no installation option is offered, the browser probably does not support PWA installation of Khartis.
sidenav_install_help_other_note: In this case, preferably use Chrome, Edge or Safari to install the application.

category_shape_mode_info: Unique: same shape for all categories. Different: one shape per category. Ordered: shapes applied according to the order of the categories.
symbol_mode_info: Choose how the symbols represent your data: fixed size, proportional to a value, grouped into classes or by category.
proportional_type_info: Single: one symbol per entity. Double: two half-symbols to compare two values.
common_scale_info: Enabled, symbols A and B share the same value → size scale and are therefore directly comparable.
symbol_a_size_according: Size of symbol A according to
symbol_b_size_according: Size of symbol B according to
break_value_info: Above this value, the main color applies; below, the secondary color. Leave empty to keep a single color.
position_mode_info: Arrangement of symbols A and B on each entity: superposition, juxtaposition or division.
size_according_info: Select the numeric variable that determines the size of each symbol.
max_size_info: Maximum size in pixels for the largest value. Lower values are proportionally reduced.
shape_info: Geometric shape used to represent each entity on the map.
scale_type_info: Method of scaling sizes. Linear for direct proportionality, Square root to mitigate discrepancies, Logarithmic for large amplitudes.
show_missing_data_info: Displays a specific symbol for entities without data, so that they remain visible on the map.
fill_section_info: Inner color of the symbols. Can be fixed, vary by class or by category.
stroke_section_info: Stroke drawn around each symbol. Allows to distinguish overlapping entities.
unique_size_info: Fixed size in pixels applied to all symbols.
category_variable_info: Select the variable whose distinct values define the color categories.
symbols_section_info: Symbols represent point entities on the map (points, circles, squares, etc.). Configure their size, shape, color and opacity.
polygons_section_info: Polygons represent surface areas on the map (regions, countries, plots, etc.). Configure the fill and stroke.
lines_section_info: Lines represent linear entities on the map (roads, borders, flows, etc.). Configure their thickness, color and style.
labels_section_info: Labels display a text associated with each entity on the map, such as a name or a value.
texts_section_info: Texts allow to add free annotations on the map, regardless of the geographic entities.
labels_disabled_no_geometry: Labels require geographic data (points, lines or polygons).
texts_disabled_no_geometry: Texts require geographic data (points, lines or polygons).
data_visualized_info: Select the dataset to use for this visualization. The suggestions adapt to the geometry type of the selected dataset.
basemap_style_info: Choose an area (France or World) and a style: Colors for general mapping, Grayscale for datavisualization, or Satellite for aerial imagery. Activate or deactivate the layer groups below.

map_projection_disabled_custom_basemap: Globe mode is not available as long as an imported or custom reference basemap is active.
basemap_tiled_info: Activates the reference background (IGN & OpenStreetMap) instead of the vector layers. Useful for the geographic context but hides the customizable layers.
geo_step_info: Georeferencing allows to locate your data on the map by associating them with known geographic entities or GPS coordinates.
geo_reference_info: Entities: associate your data with place names (countries, regions, cities). Coordinates: use latitude/longitude columns.
geo_linked_variable_info: Column of your data that contains geographic identifiers (country names, ISO codes, region names, etc.).
geo_longitude_info: Column containing longitude values (East-West coordinate, between -180 and 180).
geo_latitude_info: Column containing latitude values (North-South coordinate, between -90 and 90).
basemap_step_info: The basemap provides the geographic outlines (countries, regions, etc.) on which your data is projected. The join associates your data with the basemap.
join_assisted_info: The assisted join automatically compares the values of your geographic column with the entities of the basemap and reports uncertain matches.
enrich_step_info: Enrich your dataset by joining an external tabular file or by overlaying an additional basemap.
year_filter_no_year_columns: No numeric column found for year filtering
basemap_tiled_enabled_desc: The IGN & OpenStreetMap reference background is active. Choose a style below.
basemap_tiled_disabled_desc: Orthographic view (Deck.gl only). All layers are superimposed without a reference background.
basemap_layers_disabled_by_maplibre: Disabled when the reference background is active
basemap_layer_not_implemented: This layer is not yet implemented
basemap_layer_unavailable_reason: The active basemap does not yet provide the necessary data for this layer.
primitive_unavailable_reason: This primitive is not compatible with the data geometry or the selected visualization type.
basemap_dotted_unavailable_reason: Dotted rendering is not reliably supported for this layer on the active basemap.
deck_debug_metric_pending: No usable measurement at the moment.
deck_debug_metric_fps_info: Frames rendered per second. If the value drops during interactions, the rendering or the machine becomes the limiting factor.
deck_debug_metric_fps_state_good: Smooth rendering. The map holds the load well.
deck_debug_metric_fps_state_ok: Correct rendering. Monitor the heaviest interactions.
deck_debug_metric_fps_state_warn: Visible drop. The rendering begins to saturate.
deck_debug_metric_fps_state_bad: Slow rendering. Look for a bottleneck on the data, layers or GPU side.
deck_debug_metric_cpu_info: Average CPU time per frame on the JavaScript and Deck side. The higher it goes, the more expensive the preparation of layers and data is.
deck_debug_metric_cpu_state_good: Low CPU cost. The JS and Deck preparation remains light.
deck_debug_metric_cpu_state_ok: Moderate CPU cost. Nothing to worry about for now.
deck_debug_metric_cpu_state_warn: High CPU cost. The preparation of the layers may limit the fluidity.
deck_debug_metric_cpu_state_bad: CPU is the limiting factor. Reduce recalculations, JS treatments or the number of layers.
deck_debug_metric_gpu_info: Average GPU time per frame. A rise indicates that the WebGL drawing or the GPU composition becomes the bottleneck.
deck_debug_metric_gpu_state_good: Low GPU cost. The WebGL drawing remains light.
deck_debug_metric_gpu_state_ok: Moderate GPU cost. Monitor heavy styles and layers.
deck_debug_metric_gpu_state_warn: High GPU cost. The WebGL rendering begins to weigh.
deck_debug_metric_gpu_state_bad: GPU is the limiting factor. Simplify the drawing or the composition.
discretization_desc_kmeans: Creates natural thresholds with the K-means SQL method.
discretization_desc_quantile: Each class contains the same number of values.
discretization_desc_equal_interval: Equal size intervals between the minimum and the maximum.
discretization_desc_q6: Six classes with unequal intervals: the extreme values are isolated in the first and last classes.
discretization_desc_nested_means: Hierarchical subdivision by means. The number of classes must be a power of 2 (2, 4, 8, 16...).
discretization_desc_head_tail: Classes based on the mean, adapted to long-tailed distributions. The number of classes is self-determined; requesting more classes than the algorithm finds will use the maximum available.
discretization_error_min_greater_max: Class {classNumber}: the minimum is greater than the maximum
discretization_error_overlapping: Class {classNumber}: overlap with the previous class
